title: IonQ Stock Rises 23.4% After Record Q3 Revenue (Nov 6)
summary: IONQ closed at $32.62 on Nov 6, up 23.42%, after IonQ reported record Q3 revenue of $173.8 million and raised its 2026 revenue guidance.
body_markdown:
## Why IonQ Stock Rose


According to the[company's official release](https://investors.ionq.com/news/news-details/2026/IonQ-Announces-Record-3Q26-Revenues-and-Raises-FY2026-Guidance-to-505---515-Million-as-Backlog-Grows-to-1-2-Billion/) dated November 5, third-quarter revenue reached $173.8 million, up 336% from a year earlier and IonQ's sixth consecutive record quarter. IonQ Platform revenue rose 127% to $90.3 million, and the SkyWater Foundry Services segment added $83.5 million. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $505 million to $515 million, and its remaining performance obligations more than doubled to $1.2 billion.


As reported by TIKR, revenue came in $32 million above consensus, and the new guidance replaced a range of $450 million to $460 million, the third increase this year. TIKR tied Friday's jump to the results and reported that IonQ's 2027 Superion 256 capacity is sold out, with orders extending into 2028.


Chairman and CEO Niccolo de Masi called it "the strongest quarter in our company's history," per[The Quantum Insider](https://thequantuminsider.com/2026/11/05/ionq-raises-revenue-forecast-as-quarterly-sales-climb-to-173-8-million/) , which also reported that Nvidia will deploy a Superion 256 system at its Accelerated Quantum Research Center.


## IONQ Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Remaining performance obligations of $1.2 billion give IonQ a larger base of contracted revenue, according to the company's release.
- IonQ expects its quantum computing revenue to grow 110% this year, per the release.
- Cash, cash equivalents and investments were $1.7 billion at September 30, or about $3.7 billion pro forma after a $2.0 billion equity offering closed on October 16, per the release.


### Risks


- The adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $133.6 million from $48.9 million a year earlier, per TIKR, and the quarter's $564.0 million net income came largely from a non-cash warrant gain, according to the company.
- TIKR noted that IonQ is paying for its Elisity acquisition with up to $1.3 billion of stock, on top of the October offering, so the share count is rising.
- Lock-ups on certain shares, warrants and options expire on November 14, which TIKR said will test whether the rally can absorb new supply.
